lessons.title: Emerging Technologies Changing the World
lessons.notes_html:
What are Emerging Technologies?

Emerging technologies are the new, modern technologies that are changing the world by solving life's problems and bringing new ways of doing things.

The Book's Emerging Technologies

TechnologyWhat it does
Artificial Intelligence (AI)Teaches machines to think, learn and decide like humans
RoboticsMachines sense their surroundings with sensors, decide on their own and work
Virtual Reality (VR)Makes an artificial world feel real, through special glasses or a headset
BiometricsIdentifies people by parts of the body — fingerprints, face, eyes/iris and voice
Computer-Assisted TranslationMakes translation between languages easy
3D Holographic ImagingShows a picture (a hologram) in the air, which can be seen from all sides
Cloud ComputingGives storage, apps and software through the internet
Open-Source SoftwareAllows everyone free use and modification

Note: Banking is NOT an emerging technology in the book's list.

VR in Education

  • Students sitting in class can see historical places and experience things that are not present in front of them.
  • Training on dangerous equipment can be done safely.
  • Lessons become lively and interesting, which improves learning.

How Technology Changed Daily Life

  • Communication: landline phone (1876) → mobile phone (1990) → smartphone (after 2007). Now one phone runs the internet, photos, video, GPS, calls and learning/entertainment apps.
  • Computing: from large, expensive first-generation computers to fast, cheap fourth/fifth-generation personal computers and mobiles.
  • Daily tasks — communication, shopping, learning, entertainment, work — have become faster, easier, better and cheaper.

mcqs.q: What can we do through 3D imaging/processing?
options: Move things from one factory to another
Make a real decision about a sample
mcqs.why: Correct answer: Show a hologram. 3D images are holograms — pictures that appear in the air and can be seen from all sides. This is one of the emerging technologies in this lesson.

mcqs.q: What is possible through biometric verification?
options: Identification using face, fingerprints and voice
mcqs.why: Correct answer: Identification using face, fingerprints and voice. In biometrics a person is identified by parts of the human body — fingerprints, face, eyes/iris and voice — not by numbers or passwords.

mcqs.q: Which of the following is NOT called an emerging technology?
mcqs.why: Correct answer: Banking. The book's emerging technologies are artificial intelligence, robotics, virtual reality, biometrics, computer-assisted translation, 3D holographic imaging, cloud computing and open-source software. Banking is not among them.

mcqs.q: In robotics, how does a machine work on its own?
options: It is pushed by a person
It senses its surroundings with sensors, decides on its own and works
It only follows a remote control
It works only when connected to a printer
mcqs.why: Correct answer: It senses its surroundings with sensors, decides on its own and works. That is what makes a robot different from an ordinary machine — sensors let it feel the world around it and then it decides and acts.

mcqs.q: What does Virtual Reality (VR) do?
options: It creates an artificial world that feels real, through special glasses or a headset
It stores files on the internet
mcqs.why: Correct answer: It creates an artificial world that feels real. VR is used through special glasses or a headset, and in education it lets students visit historical places and train safely on dangerous equipment.

mcqs.q: What does cloud computing give us through the internet?
mcqs.why: Correct answer: Storage, apps and software. Cloud computing provides these through the internet, so we do not need everything stored on our own computer.

mcqs.q: What is special about open-source software?
options: Only one company may use it
Everyone can use it freely and modify it
It works only without the internet
mcqs.why: Correct answer: Everyone can use it freely and modify it. Open-source software allows free use and modification by everyone — that is why it is in the book's list of emerging technologies.

mcqs.q: How does artificial intelligence help machines?
options: It connects machines to a printer
It teaches machines to think, learn and decide like humans
It stores machines in the cloud
mcqs.why: Correct answer: It teaches machines to think, learn and decide like humans. AI is one of the main emerging technologies that are changing the world.

mcqs.q: Which of these is a use of VR in education?
options: Students can train safely on dangerous equipment
Students can save files in the cloud
mcqs.why: Correct answer: Students can train safely on dangerous equipment. VR also lets students see historical places from the classroom and makes lessons lively and interesting, which improves learning.

mcqs.q: How has communication changed with time, according to the lesson?
options: Phones have not changed at all
From landline phone (1876) to mobile phone (1990) and then smartphone (after 2007)
mcqs.why: Correct answer: Landline phone (1876) → mobile phone (1990) → smartphone (after 2007). Today one smartphone runs the internet, photos, video, GPS, calls and apps — technology made everything faster, easier and cheaper.

lessons.title: Peripheral Devices and Ports
lessons.notes_html:
Peripheral Devices

A peripheral device is an external hardware device that gives the computer additional functionality. Peripheral devices give input to the system unit and take output from it. The computer (CPU) alone can do only limited work, so peripherals are necessary.

TypeJobExamples
Input devicesSend data into the computerKeyboard, mouse, webcam, scanner
Output devicesShow the resultMonitor, printer, speaker, projector
Storage devicesSave dataUSB drive, external hard drive, SSD
Network devicesConnect to the internet and networksModem, wireless access point, network card

Ports

Ports are the connections (physical connection points) on the front or back of the computer case that allow us to plug in I/O devices.

  • USB port — the most common port; mouse, keyboard, printer, scanner and hard drive connect through it and data transfers quickly. The first non-commercial USB port was released in 1994.
  • HDMI port — connects the computer to a monitor or projector so clear video and sound are obtained.
  • Ethernet port — for the network cable.

Printer vs Scanner

Printer (Output)Scanner (Input)
Converts the computer's information into a hard copy on paper — prints text and pictures (homework, reports, letters)Copies things using light and converts paper into digital files, which can be saved and shared
Computer → paperPaper → computer

mcqs.q: Which input/output port is most commonly used to connect devices like a USB drive, mouse and printer to the computer?
mcqs.why: Correct answer: USB port. The mouse, keyboard, printer, scanner and hard drive are connected through the USB port, and data transfers quickly through it.

mcqs.q: What is the main purpose of peripheral devices?
options: To connect only to the internet
To give the computer additional functionality
mcqs.why: Correct answer: To give the computer additional functionality. A peripheral is an external hardware device that provides additional functionality to the computer — input, output, storage or networking.

mcqs.q: Devices like the mouse and keyboard are connected to the computer through ______.
mcqs.why: Correct answer: Ports. Ports are the physical connection points on the computer to which devices are connected.

mcqs.q: The ______ port is used to connect a projector to the computer.
mcqs.why: Correct answer: HDMI. The computer is connected to a monitor or projector through the HDMI port so that clear video and sound are obtained.

mcqs.q: ______ devices are devices that give input to the system unit and take output from it.
mcqs.why: Correct answer: Peripheral. Peripheral devices give the computer additional functionality, such as input devices (keyboard, mouse), output devices (monitor, printer), storage and network devices.

mcqs.q: ______ are the connections on the front or back of the computer case that allow us to plug in I/O devices.
mcqs.why: Correct answer: Ports. I/O devices plug into ports, such as USB, HDMI and Ethernet ports, which are found on the front or back of the computer case.

mcqs.q: The first non-commercial USB port was released in ______.
mcqs.why: Correct answer: 1994. According to the book, the USB port was introduced in 1994 and became the most common way to connect devices.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between a printer and a scanner?
options: A printer converts computer information to paper; a scanner converts paper into digital files
A printer is an input device, a scanner is an output device
mcqs.why: Correct answer: The printer goes from computer to paper (output — a hard copy), while the scanner goes from paper to computer (input — it copies things using light and makes digital files that can be saved and shared).

mcqs.q: Which of these is a network device?
mcqs.why: Correct answer: Modem. Network devices — modem, wireless access point and network card — connect the computer to the internet and networks. The others are input/output devices.

mcqs.q: Why are peripheral devices necessary for the computer?
options: They are needed only for games
They increase the weight of the computer
They make the computer case colourful
Without them the computer cannot take data in, show results, save files or connect
mcqs.why: Correct answer: Without peripherals the computer can do only limited work. Input devices send data in, output devices show results, storage devices save data and network devices connect it — all of these are necessary.

lessons.title: Technology Around Us — Activities
lessons.notes_html:
Activity 1 — Robot Model and Hologram

  • Group B — holographic image: a 3D picture that appears in the air and can be seen from all sides, formed by rays of light. Example: a hologram in a clothing shop.

Activity 2 — New Technologies at Home and School

At homeAt school

Class Activity — I/O Ports in the Library

Name of I/O portName of peripheral device

mcqs.q: In the class activity, Group A made a paper model of a robot. What is a robot?
options: A machine that senses its surroundings with sensors, decides on its own and works
A machine that only prints pictures
A machine that must be pushed by hand
mcqs.why: Correct answer: A machine that senses with sensors, decides on its own and works. Examples from the activity: a robot arm in a factory and a vacuum-cleaner robot at home.

mcqs.q: A holographic image is:
options: A picture saved in the cloud
A 3D picture that appears in the air and can be seen from all sides
mcqs.why: Correct answer: A 3D picture in the air, seen from all sides. It is formed by rays of light — for example, a hologram in a clothing shop.

mcqs.q: Which of these is an example of new technology at school?
mcqs.why: Correct answer: CCTV cameras. The activity's school list is: computer lab, CCTV cameras, projector, smart board and printer. The others were in the home list.

mcqs.q: What does a modem do?
options: It shows pictures on the screen
It converts the computer's data into phone-line signals and back
mcqs.why: Correct answer: It converts data into phone-line signals and back. The modem works between the computer and the Internet Service Provider (ISP) and connects the computer to the internet.

mcqs.q: What is special about a NIC card?
options: It is a card fixed on the motherboard and gives the computer an identity on the network
It is kept outside the computer case
mcqs.why: Correct answer: It is fixed on the motherboard and gives the computer an identity on the network. The NIC card connects the computer to a network.

mcqs.q: What is common between a modem and a NIC card?
options: Both are network devices that help connect the computer to the internet/network
mcqs.why: Correct answer: Both are network devices. In the Venn diagram activity, this similarity goes in the overlapping middle part of the two circles.

mcqs.q: Which port is used for a network cable (router)?
mcqs.why: Correct answer: Ethernet port. From the library observation table: Ethernet port — network cable (router); HDMI — monitor/projector; audio jack — headphones/speaker; power port — charger.

mcqs.q: A pen drive is connected through which port?
mcqs.why: Correct answer: USB port. In the class activity table, the USB port's devices are mouse, keyboard, printer and pen drive.

mcqs.q: Headphones and speakers are connected through:
mcqs.why: Correct answer: Audio jack. The library activity table lists headphones and speaker with the audio jack.

mcqs.q: The ISP in the modem activity means:
options: Internet Service Provider — the company between the computer and the internet
mcqs.why: Correct answer: Internet Service Provider. The modem works between the computer and the ISP to connect the computer to the internet.

lessons.title: Microsoft Word — Files, Views and Shortcuts
lessons.notes_html:
Microsoft Word — a Word Processor

Microsoft Word is a word processor — software used to create, edit, format and print documents. With MS Word we can make letters, reports, assignments, projects, CVs, notes, books and forms. It has facilities for fonts, pictures, tables, headers/footers and spell check.

File Extensions

ProgramFile extension
MS Word (default).docx
MS PowerPoint.ppt (newer format: .pptx)

PowerPoint Views

A PowerPoint presentation can be seen in these viewing formats:

  • Slide view
  • Outline view
  • Slide show view

“Presentation view” is NOT a viewing format of PowerPoint.

Important Shortcuts (MS Word)

ShortcutWork
Ctrl + NCreate a new blank document
Ctrl + SSave the document immediately
Ctrl + PPrint

mcqs.q: What is Microsoft Word?
mcqs.why: Correct answer: Word processor. A word processor is software used to create, edit, format and print documents — that is exactly what MS Word does.

mcqs.q: The default extension of an MS Word file is ______.
mcqs.why: Correct answer: .docx. The default extension of an MS Word file is .docx — it appears at the end of every Word file's name.

mcqs.q: The extension of an MS PowerPoint file is ______.
mcqs.why: Correct answer: .ppt. The extension of a PowerPoint file is .ppt (in the newer format it is .pptx).

mcqs.q: Which of the following is NOT a viewing format for a PowerPoint presentation?
mcqs.why: Correct answer: Presentation view. PowerPoint's viewing formats are Slide view, Outline view and Slide show view; “Presentation view” is not one of them.

mcqs.q: Which keyboard shortcut is used to save a document immediately?
mcqs.why: Correct answer: Ctrl + S. Pressing Ctrl + S saves the document at once, so our work is not lost.

mcqs.q: The shortcut key for creating a new document in MS Word is ______.
mcqs.why: Correct answer: Ctrl + N. Ctrl + N creates a new blank document in MS Word (N = New).

mcqs.q: Which of these can be made with MS Word?
mcqs.why: Correct answer: Letters, reports, assignments and CVs. MS Word is used to create, edit, format and print documents such as letters, reports, projects, notes, books and forms.

mcqs.q: What is the shortcut for printing a document?
mcqs.why: Correct answer: Ctrl + P. P stands for Print. Remember the set: Ctrl + N = New, Ctrl + S = Save, Ctrl + P = Print.

mcqs.q: A word processor is software used to:
options: Create, edit, format and print documents
mcqs.why: Correct answer: Create, edit, format and print documents. That is the definition of a word processor, and MS Word is the example in this lesson.

mcqs.q: In the newer format, a PowerPoint file's extension is:
mcqs.why: Correct answer: .pptx. The book gives .ppt as the PowerPoint extension, and the newer format is .pptx — just as Word's is .docx.

lessons.title: Working in MS Word
lessons.notes_html:
The Ribbon and Tabs

In MS Word the ribbon is divided into different sections called tabs — such as Home, Insert, Design and Layout. The Header and Footer option is found in the Insert tab.

Checking Mistakes

Mistakes in MS Word can be checked using the spell check facility, which checks the spelling and grammar mistakes in a document.

Save and Save As

Save (Ctrl + S)Save As (Alt + F + A)
Saves changes in the same fileSaves the same file as a copy with a new name, new location or new format; the original file stays unchanged
—Example: saving a document as a PDF

Basic Functions of MS Word

  • Creating a new document (Ctrl + N)
  • Typing and editing text
  • Formatting — bold, italic, underline, font size and colour
  • Spell check
  • Saving (Ctrl + S) and Save As
  • Printing (Ctrl + P)
  • Inserting pictures, tables and pages
  • Adding headers and footers
  • Find and replace, and word count

mcqs.q: In which tab is the Header and Footer option found?
mcqs.why: Correct answer: Insert. Header and Footer is found in the Insert tab of MS Word — headers and footers are inserted into the document from there.

mcqs.q: In MS Word the ribbon is divided into different sections called ______.
mcqs.why: Correct answer: Tabs. The ribbon has tabs such as Home, Insert, Design, Layout, etc., and each tab holds its own tools.

mcqs.q: Mistakes in MS Word can be checked using the ______ facility.
mcqs.why: Correct answer: Spell check. With spell check, the spelling and grammar mistakes in a document can be checked and corrected.

mcqs.q: Use ______ in MS Word to make a copy of a file.
mcqs.why: Correct answer: Save As. With Save As, a copy of the same file is saved with a new name, new location or new format (such as PDF).

mcqs.q: What is the difference between Save and Save As?
options: Save keeps changes in the same file; Save As saves a copy with a new name, location or format
Save is used only for pictures
mcqs.why: Correct answer: Save (Ctrl + S) saves changes in the same file, while Save As (Alt + F + A) saves a copy with a new name, new location or new format — the original stays unchanged.

mcqs.q: Which of these is a basic function of MS Word?
options: Formatting text — bold, italic, underline, font size and colour
mcqs.why: Correct answer: Formatting text. The basic functions of MS Word include typing and editing, formatting, spell check, saving, printing, inserting pictures/tables and find and replace.

mcqs.q: Find and Replace in MS Word is used to:
options: Find a word in the document and replace it with another word
mcqs.why: Correct answer: Find a word and replace it. Find and Replace is one of the basic functions of MS Word, along with word count.

mcqs.q: The shortcut for Save As given in the book is:
mcqs.why: Correct answer: Alt + F + A. Save is Ctrl + S, but Save As — saving a copy with a new name, location or format — is Alt + F + A in the book.

mcqs.q: Headers and footers in a document appear:
options: At the top (header) and bottom (footer) of the pages
Only in the middle of the page
Only on the first page picture
mcqs.why: Correct answer: At the top and bottom of the pages. That is why the option sits in the Insert tab — we insert them once and they appear on the pages.

mcqs.q: Which tab is NOT named as a ribbon tab in this lesson?
mcqs.why: Correct answer: Games. The ribbon tabs named in the book are Home, Insert, Design, Layout and others like them — there is no Games tab in MS Word.

lessons.title: Presentations and Email
lessons.notes_html:
Multimedia Presentation

The purpose of a multimedia presentation is to present information with text, pictures, sound, video and animation in such a way that the viewer understands easily, pays attention and remembers. Examples: a lesson presentation in class, a business report, introducing a project.

Email Terms

TermMeaning
Email addressA person's unique address on which email can be sent and received, e.g. user@example.com (username @ domain)
PasswordA secret code (letters + numbers + symbols, e.g. John@123) that keeps the email account safe; it must not be told to anyone
ContactA person's saved information including their email address, so that they can be contacted easily

Uses of an email address: sending/receiving messages, creating accounts, recovering accounts, notifications, and sending documents.

Inbox, Sent and Spam

FolderPurpose
InboxThe emails we have received appear here
SentThe emails we have sent are saved here
SpamUnwanted/junk emails (adverts, fraud) that are automatically separated and filtered

mcqs.q: What is the purpose of a multimedia presentation?
options: To save files on the computer
To present information with text, pictures, sound, video and animation so the viewer understands easily and remembers
mcqs.why: Correct answer: To present information so the viewer understands easily, pays attention and remembers. Multimedia means using text, pictures, sound, video and animation together — like a lesson presentation in class.

mcqs.q: An email address is:
options: A person's unique address for sending and receiving email, e.g. user@example.com
mcqs.why: Correct answer: A unique address for sending and receiving email. It is made of a username, the @ sign and a domain, like user@example.com.

mcqs.q: A password must be:
options: The same as our name only
A secret code of letters, numbers and symbols, told to no one
mcqs.why: Correct answer: A secret code told to no one. A password like John@123 (letters + numbers + symbols) keeps the email account safe.

mcqs.q: A 'contact' in email means:
options: A person's saved information including their email address, so they can be contacted easily
mcqs.why: Correct answer: A person's saved information including their email address. Saving contacts makes it easy to contact people again.

mcqs.q: The emails we have received appear in the:
mcqs.why: Correct answer: Inbox. Received emails come to the Inbox; the emails we send are saved in Sent.

mcqs.q: Unwanted/junk emails like adverts and fraud are put in:
mcqs.why: Correct answer: Spam. Spam emails are automatically separated and filtered so they do not mix with our real mail.

mcqs.q: Which of these is a use of an email address?
mcqs.why: Correct answer: Recovering an account. The lesson lists: sending/receiving messages, creating accounts, recovering accounts, notifications and sending documents.

mcqs.q: The emails we have sent are saved in:
mcqs.why: Correct answer: Sent. Every email we send is saved in the Sent folder, so we can check it later.

mcqs.q: In the email address user@example.com, the part before @ is the:
mcqs.why: Correct answer: Username. An email address is username @ domain — the username is the person's own name part and the domain is the service part.

mcqs.q: Which is an example of a multimedia presentation?
options: A plain text file with no pictures
A class lesson presentation with text, pictures, sound and video
mcqs.why: Correct answer: A class lesson presentation. Multimedia presentations combine text, pictures, sound, video and animation — other examples are a business report and introducing a project.

lessons.title: Digital Skills Activities
lessons.notes_html:
Activity 1 — Document: “My Best Friend” (MS Word)

  • Write the title and centre it; use WordArt from the Insert tab.
  • Write a paragraph: your friend's name, class, and what you like most about him/her (e.g. truthful, helpful, studies together).
  • Make the document colourful and well-arranged (font, colour, picture) using the Insert, Design and Layout tabs, and save it with Ctrl + S.

Activity 2 — PowerPoint: “My Dream Vacation” (8 steps)

  • Open PowerPoint, choose a blank presentation; make 4 slides (title, place, things to do, summary).
  • Add a theme from the Design tab; add transitions (Transitions tab → Fade) and animations (Wipe, Zoom).
  • Insert pictures (at least one per slide); add footer/header from Insert → Header and Footer → Apply to All.
  • Review the show with F5 (Esc to stop) and save with File → Save As.

Class Activities

  • Word documents: birthday invitation, party theme, school timetable — title in WordArt, text, a table (e.g. guest list), colourful design, save.
  • PowerPoint test: slides on geometric shapes (triangle, square, rectangle, circle — picture + name + number of sides); a poem with each line animated with a different effect (Appear, Fly In, Zoom).
  • Creating an email account (Gmail): Create account → name → username (e.g. jane123@gmail.com) → strong password → phone number → verification code. A professional username and strong password keep the account safe and identifiable.
  • Sending an email: To (friend), Cc (teacher, for information), Bcc (hidden recipient), Subject, content, signature — and attach a file before sending.

mcqs.q: In the 'My Best Friend' document activity, the title is made beautiful using:
mcqs.why: Correct answer: WordArt from the Insert tab. The activity steps are: write the title, centre it, use WordArt, write the paragraph, and save with Ctrl + S.

mcqs.q: In the PowerPoint activity, transitions like Fade are added from the:
mcqs.why: Correct answer: Transitions tab. In the model project, all slides are selected and the Fade transition is applied with duration 01.00.

mcqs.q: To start a slide show and review it, we press:
mcqs.why: Correct answer: F5. Press F5 to run the show, click to show each animation slowly, and press Esc to stop.

mcqs.q: In an email, the 'Cc' field is used for:
options: Sending a copy to someone for information, e.g. the teacher
mcqs.why: Correct answer: Sending a copy for information. In the class activity the teacher's address goes in Cc; To is the main receiver and Bcc is the hidden recipient.

mcqs.q: While creating an email account, why should the password be strong?
mcqs.why: Correct answer: To keep the account safe. The activity teaches choosing a professional username (your own name) and a strong password of letters, numbers and symbols.

mcqs.q: A file can be sent along with an email by using:
mcqs.why: Correct answer: Attach file. The sending-email activity ends with: attach a file → Send.

mcqs.q: In the geometric-shapes PowerPoint activity, each shape's slide shows:
mcqs.why: Correct answer: Picture + name + number of sides. The shapes are triangle, square, rectangle and circle, and the poem's lines each get a different animation.

mcqs.q: The footer text is added to all slides through:
options: Insert → Header and Footer → Apply to All
mcqs.why: Correct answer: Insert → Header and Footer → Apply to All. In the model project the footer 'Ali Khan — 7-B' is applied to every slide this way.

mcqs.q: A birthday invitation document in MS Word can include:
options: A guest-list table, colourful font, picture and border
mcqs.why: Correct answer: A guest-list table with colourful design. The class activity designs the invitation with WordArt title, text, table, picture and border, then saves it.

mcqs.q: The verification code step comes while:
options: Creating an email account — after entering the phone number
mcqs.why: Correct answer: Creating an email account. The steps are: Create account → name → username → strong password → phone number → enter the verification code.

lessons.title: Computational Thinking
lessons.notes_html:
Computational Thinking

According to the book, the parts of computational thinking are:

  • Decomposition — breaking a big problem into small parts (e.g. breaking a puzzle into pieces and edges).
  • Abstraction — ignoring unnecessary information and keeping only what matters.
  • Logical thinking — putting steps in a clear order.
  • Decision making — choosing what to do by rules and conditions.

Estimation is NOT a part of computational thinking.

What is an Algorithm?

An algorithm is the process of arranging a plan in a clear and step-by-step order — a finite and clear sequence of step-by-step instructions for solving a problem. There can be many ways to solve the same problem.

Correct and Incorrect Data

Data must make sense: an age of -5 is NOT correct, because age can never be negative. Testing with correct and incorrect data is part of solving a problem properly.

Algorithmic Thinking in Real Life

Algorithmic thinking is important not only on computers but also in real life: breaking a problem into small parts, recognising patterns, taking steps in order and checking the result.

  • Making a cake: gather the ingredients → mix them → bake → taste (validation).
  • Getting ready for school: clothes, bag, breakfast, route — in order.

mcqs.q: Which of the following is NOT a part of computational thinking?
mcqs.why: Correct answer: Estimation. According to the book, the parts of computational thinking are decomposition (breaking down), abstraction, logical thinking and decision making; estimation is not among them.

mcqs.q: Which of the following is NOT a correct age?
mcqs.why: Correct answer: -5. Age can never be negative, so -5 is incorrect data — this example is used in the lesson for testing algorithms.

mcqs.q: Which of the following is an example of decomposition?
options: Solving a puzzle all at once
Breaking a puzzle into pieces and edges
mcqs.why: Correct answer: Breaking a puzzle into pieces and edges. Decomposition means breaking a big problem into small parts so each part becomes easy.

mcqs.q: ______ is the process of arranging a plan in a clear and step-by-step order.
mcqs.why: Correct answer: Algorithm. An algorithm is a finite and clear sequence of step-by-step instructions for solving a problem.

mcqs.q: There can be ______ ways to solve a problem.
mcqs.why: Correct answer: Many. The same problem can be solved in many ways — we choose a clear and correct one.

mcqs.q: Abstraction in computational thinking means:
options: Ignoring unnecessary information and keeping only what matters
mcqs.why: Correct answer: Ignoring unnecessary information. In the class-monitor election example, abstraction means ignoring things like favourite colour and keeping only the voter list, candidates' names and votes.

mcqs.q: Which is an example of algorithmic thinking in daily life?
options: Making a cake: gather ingredients, mix, bake, then taste
mcqs.why: Correct answer: Making a cake in ordered steps. Algorithmic thinking — small parts, patterns, steps in order, checking the result — is useful in daily life, not only on computers.

mcqs.q: In the cake example, tasting the cake at the end is like:
mcqs.why: Correct answer: Validation — checking the result. After following the steps, we check whether the result is correct, just as we taste the cake.

mcqs.q: Decision making in computational thinking means:
options: Choosing what to do by rules and conditions
mcqs.why: Correct answer: Choosing by rules and conditions. For example, in an election: one vote per student, secret ballot, re-voting on a tie.

mcqs.q: Getting ready for school — clothes, bag, breakfast, route — shows:
options: Steps taken in a clear order
mcqs.why: Correct answer: Steps in a clear order. This is algorithmic thinking in real life: the order of steps matters, just like in an algorithm.

RectangleA process or step (such as a calculation)
ParallelogramInput or Output (Print)
DiamondA decision — checking a condition

Loops

There are two types of loops:

  • Finite loop — repeats a fixed number of times or until a condition ends it, then stops.
  • Infinite loop — keeps repeating and never stops on its own.

Loops vs Conditional Statements

Conditional statement (if/else)Loop
Chooses one path on the basis of a condition; that step runs once — selectionRepeats the same instructions again and again while a condition stays true — repetition

The If-Else-If statement allows checking many conditions, one by one.

Testing an Algorithm (Validation)

  • An algorithm must be tested with correct and incorrect data to make sure it produces correct results in all cases — this is called validation.
  • Example: in checking age, both 12 (correct) and -5 (incorrect) are tried. If a wrong result is found, the steps are corrected.
  • If we change the steps of the algorithm, the flowchart must also be changed with the same symbols, and checked (validated) again — otherwise it becomes wrong.

mcqs.q: Which symbol is used to show the start or end of a flowchart?
mcqs.why: Correct answer: Oval. The oval (terminal) symbol shows the start and end of a flowchart.

mcqs.q: The ______ symbol is used to represent a process in a flowchart.
mcqs.why: Correct answer: Rectangle. The rectangle represents a process or step, such as a calculation like Sum = A + B + C.

mcqs.q: There are ______ types of loops.
mcqs.why: Correct answer: Two. A finite loop stops after its work ends; an infinite loop keeps repeating and never stops on its own.

mcqs.q: The ______ statement allows checking many conditions.
mcqs.why: Correct answer: If-Else-If. This statement checks more than one condition one by one, e.g. hot, cold or normal temperature.

mcqs.q: Why is it necessary to test an algorithm with correct and incorrect data?
options: To make sure the algorithm produces correct results in all cases
mcqs.why: Correct answer: To make sure it produces correct results in all cases. This testing is called validation — e.g. trying age 12 (correct) and -5 (incorrect).

mcqs.q: How are loops different from conditional statements?
options: A conditional chooses one path and runs once; a loop repeats instructions again and again
mcqs.why: Correct answer: Conditional = selection (once), loop = repetition (again and again). A conditional statement chooses one path on the basis of a condition; a loop repeats while a condition stays true.

mcqs.q: If we change the steps of the algorithm, what must happen to the flowchart?
options: The flowchart must also be changed with the same symbols and validated again
mcqs.why: Correct answer: The flowchart must also be changed and validated again. Every changed step must be changed in the flowchart with the same symbol, so the two stay identical.

mcqs.q: Which flowchart symbol is used for a decision (checking a condition)?
mcqs.why: Correct answer: Diamond. The diamond holds a question like 'Password = SECRET?' with Yes and No paths coming out of it.

mcqs.q: Input and Print steps in a flowchart are shown with a:
mcqs.why: Correct answer: Parallelogram. In the book's flowcharts, Input A, B, C and Print Sum are both drawn as parallelograms.

mcqs.q: Testing an algorithm with different inputs, like 12 and -5 for age, is called:
mcqs.why: Correct answer: Validation. It verifies that correct data gives the correct result and incorrect data does not break the algorithm; if a wrong result is found, the steps are corrected.

lessons.title: Making Flowcharts
lessons.notes_html:
Flowchart 1 — Sum of Three Numbers

Start (oval) → Input A, B, C (parallelogram) → Sum = A + B + C (rectangle) → Print Sum (parallelogram) → End (oval).

Flowchart 2 — Password Check

Start (oval) → Input Password (parallelogram) → Decision (diamond): Password = "SECRET"? → Yes → Print "Access granted to you" → End; No → Print "Access denied to you!" → End.

Flowchart 3 — Sum of the First 10 Natural Numbers (Loop)

Start (oval) → N = 1, Sum = 0 (rectangle) → Decision (diamond): N ≤ 10? → Yes → Sum = Sum + N; N = N + 1 (rectangle) → back to the decision; No → Print Sum (parallelogram) → End (oval).

Flowchart 4 — Counting from 0 up to the Entered Number (Loop)

Start (oval) → Input N (parallelogram) → Count = 0 (rectangle) → Decision (diamond): Count ≤ N? → Yes → Print Count; Count = Count + 1 (rectangle) → back to the decision; No → End (oval).

Remember: a loop flowchart always has an arrow going back to the decision diamond; the loop ends when the condition becomes false.

mcqs.q: In the flowchart for the sum of three numbers, the step 'Sum = A + B + C' is drawn as a:
mcqs.why: Correct answer: Rectangle. Adding the numbers is a process (calculation), and processes are drawn as rectangles.

mcqs.q: In the password flowchart, what happens if the password is not 'SECRET'?
mcqs.why: Correct answer: 'Access denied to you!' is printed. The diamond checks Password = 'SECRET'? — Yes gives access granted, No gives access denied, then End.

mcqs.q: In the sum of the first 10 natural numbers flowchart, the loop continues while:
mcqs.why: Correct answer: N ≤ 10. Each round adds N to Sum and increases N by 1; when N becomes greater than 10, the loop stops and Sum is printed.

mcqs.q: In the counting flowchart, Count starts from:
mcqs.why: Correct answer: 0. Count = 0, then while Count ≤ N it prints Count and adds 1, so it prints 0, 1, 2, ... up to N.

mcqs.q: What makes flowcharts 3 and 4 loops?
options: An arrow goes back to the decision diamond so steps repeat
mcqs.why: Correct answer: The arrow back to the decision. The Yes path returns to the diamond (N ≤ 10? / Count ≤ N?), so the steps repeat until the condition becomes false.

mcqs.q: The first step of every flowchart in this lesson is:
mcqs.why: Correct answer: Start, drawn as an oval. Every flowchart begins with Start (oval) and finishes with End (oval).

mcqs.q: In the sum-of-three-numbers flowchart, 'Input A, B, C' uses which symbol?
mcqs.why: Correct answer: Parallelogram. Input and output (Print) steps are both shown with parallelograms in a flowchart.

mcqs.q: If N = 5 is entered in the counting flowchart, the output will be:
mcqs.why: Correct answer: 0 1 2 3 4 5. Count starts at 0 and is printed each round while Count ≤ 5, increasing by 1 every time.

mcqs.q: The final Sum printed by the first-10-natural-numbers flowchart is:
mcqs.why: Correct answer: 55. The loop adds 1 + 2 + 3 + ... + 10 = 55, and prints Sum when N passes 10.

mcqs.q: In the password flowchart, the diamond contains:
mcqs.why: Correct answer: The question Password = 'SECRET'? A diamond always holds a condition with two ways out — Yes and No.

lessons.title: Writing Algorithms
lessons.notes_html:
Algorithm 1 — Even, Odd or Zero

  • Step 1: Start. Step 2: Input number N. Step 3: If N = 0, print "Zero". Step 4: Else if N % 2 = 0, print "Even". Step 5: Else print "Odd". Step 6: End.

Algorithm 2 — 10% Discount on a Book

  • Step 1: Start. Step 2: Input the book price P. Step 3: Discount = P × 0.10. Step 4: Final Price = P − Discount. Step 5: Print Final Price. Step 6: End.
  • Example: price 1000 rupees → discount = 1000 × 0.10 = 100 rupees → final price = 1000 − 100 = 900 rupees.

Algorithm 3 — Zawiyar's Bookshop (20% Discount Rule)

  • If the price of a book is more than 500 rupees, OR Zawiyar is a student, he gets a 20 percent discount; otherwise no discount.
  • Step 3: If P > 500 OR Student = Yes, then Discount = P × 0.20; Final Price = P − Discount; print Final Price. Step 4: Else print P (no discount).

Algorithm 4 — Print a Name 10 Times (Loop)

  • Step 1: Start. Step 2: Input Name. Step 3: Set Count = 1. Step 4: If Count ≤ 10, print Name; Count = Count + 1; repeat Step 4. Step 5: End.

mcqs.q: In the Even/Odd/Zero algorithm, if N = 0, the output is:
mcqs.why: Correct answer: Zero. The algorithm checks N = 0 first; only then does it test N % 2 = 0 for Even, otherwise Odd.

mcqs.q: A number N is Even when:
mcqs.why: Correct answer: N % 2 = 0. The % sign gives the remainder after dividing by 2; remainder 0 means the number is Even.

mcqs.q: A book costs 1000 rupees. After a 10% discount, the final price is:
mcqs.why: Correct answer: 900 rupees. Discount = 1000 × 0.10 = 100 rupees; Final Price = 1000 − 100 = 900 rupees.

mcqs.q: The 10 percent discount is calculated by:
mcqs.why: Correct answer: Multiplying by 0.10. Then the discount is subtracted from the original price to get the final price.

mcqs.q: Zawiyar gets a 20% discount when:
options: The price is more than 500 rupees OR he is a student
The book costs less than 100 rupees
mcqs.why: Correct answer: Price more than 500 rupees OR student = Yes. If either condition is true, Discount = P × 0.20; otherwise no discount is given.

mcqs.q: If Zawiyar is not a student and the book costs 400 rupees, he will get:
mcqs.why: Correct answer: No discount. 400 is not more than 500 and he is not a student, so the Else part runs and the full price P is printed.

mcqs.q: In the name-printing algorithm, the loop stops when:
mcqs.why: Correct answer: When Count becomes greater than 10. Count starts at 1 and increases by 1 after each printing, so the name prints exactly 10 times.

mcqs.q: In the discount algorithm, 'P' stands for:
mcqs.why: Correct answer: The book price. Step 2 inputs the book price P, then Discount = P × 0.10 and Final Price = P − Discount.

mcqs.q: Which step comes first in every algorithm of this lesson?
mcqs.why: Correct answer: Start. Step 1 is always Start and the last step is End — clear instructions need both.

mcqs.q: If a book costs 600 rupees and Zawiyar is not a student, his discount is:
options: No discount, because 600 is less than 500
20% discount, because the price is more than 500 rupees
mcqs.why: Correct answer: 20% discount. The rule is price more than 500 OR student — 600 > 500 is true, so Discount = 600 × 0.20 = 120 rupees.

lessons.title: Algorithmic Thinking Activities
lessons.notes_html:
Activity 1 — Class Monitor Election (Computational Thinking)

PartIn the election
DecompositionBreak the problem into parts: nomination, voting, counting, announcement
AbstractionIgnore unnecessary information (favourite colour, etc.); keep only the voter list, candidates' names and votes
Logical thinkingClear order: announcement → nomination → voting → counting → announcement
Decision makingRules: one vote per student, secret ballot, re-voting on a tie
ValidationTest with sample votes that the counting is correct

Activity 2 — Clear vs Unclear Instructions

Clear instructions for Even/Odd: 1. Start. 2. Input number N. 3. If N % 2 = 0 show "Even". 4. Else show "Odd". 5. End.

The unclear version ("Take a number. Decide whether it is equal or odd. Show the result.") is unclear because it does not say HOW to decide — no clear rule (N % 2 = 0) is given; there is no start/end; and it is not clear in which case to show the result. Clear instructions give every step, condition and result with the correct number and order.

Class Activity — Total Tax Flowchart

Start (oval) → Input mouse price P1 (parallelogram) → Input keyboard price P2 (parallelogram) → Tax1 = P1 × 0.10 (rectangle) → Tax2 = P2 × 0.10 (rectangle) → Total Tax = Tax1 + Tax2 (rectangle) → Print Total Tax (parallelogram) → End (oval).

Class Activity — Finite or Infinite Loops?

  • Watering the plant until the soil is wet — Finite (stops when the soil is wet).
  • Testing a game until the player's health reaches Zero — Finite.
  • A program keeps checking new emails continuously — Infinite (never stops on its own).
  • A traffic light changes colours during the day — Finite (repeats during the day, off at night).
  • A robot waters 3 plants one after another — Finite (exactly 3 plants, then end).

Class Activity — Which Condition? If / If-Else / If-Else-If

  • "If the password is correct, log in; otherwise show an error" — If-Else.
  • "If the user clicks Submit, save the form" — If.
  • "Temperature more than 40°C → heat warning; less than 10°C → cold warning; otherwise normal" — If-Else-If-Else.
  • Note: none of the ten given examples clearly matches an "Or" (OR) condition.

mcqs.q: In the class-monitor election, breaking the problem into nomination, voting, counting and announcement is:
mcqs.why: Correct answer: Decomposition. The election problem is broken into small parts — nomination, voting, counting, announcement — so it becomes true, fair, simple and well-organised.

mcqs.q: Keeping only the voter list, candidates' names and votes (and ignoring favourite colour) is:
mcqs.why: Correct answer: Abstraction. Abstraction ignores unnecessary information and keeps only what matters for the problem.

mcqs.q: Testing the counting with sample votes in the election is:
mcqs.why: Correct answer: Validation. We test with sample votes that the counting is correct before the real election.

mcqs.q: Why are the instructions 'Take a number. Decide whether it is equal or odd.' unclear?
options: They give no clear rule (like N % 2 = 0) for deciding, and no start/end
mcqs.why: Correct answer: No clear rule is given. Clear instructions give every step, condition and result with the correct number and order — the unclear version does not say HOW to decide.

mcqs.q: 'A computer program keeps checking new emails continuously' is an example of:
mcqs.why: Correct answer: An infinite loop. The program never stops on its own — it keeps checking again and again.

mcqs.q: 'A robot waters 3 plants one after another' is:
options: A finite loop — exactly 3 plants, then end
mcqs.why: Correct answer: A finite loop. It repeats exactly 3 times and then ends — finite loops always stop.

mcqs.q: In the total tax flowchart, Tax1 is calculated as:
mcqs.why: Correct answer: P1 × 0.10. Tax on the mouse = price × 0.10, tax on the keyboard = P2 × 0.10, and Total Tax = Tax1 + Tax2.

mcqs.q: 'If the password is correct, then log in; otherwise show an error message' is:
mcqs.why: Correct answer: If-Else. There are two branches: log in (condition true) or error message (otherwise).

mcqs.q: The temperature example (heat warning / cold warning / normal) uses:
mcqs.why: Correct answer: If-Else-If-Else. More than 40°C → heat warning; else if less than 10°C → cold warning; else → normal. Three cases need the If-Else-If chain.

mcqs.q: 'Keep watering the plant until the soil becomes wet' is a finite loop because:
options: It stops when the soil becomes wet
mcqs.why: Correct answer: It stops when the soil becomes wet. A loop with a clear ending condition is finite — like the game that ends when health reaches Zero.

lessons.title: Binary Numbers and Computer Memory
lessons.notes_html:
How Information is Stored

The computer stores information in binary (0 and 1): with encoding, letters, pictures and sound are converted into binary code and that code is stored in memory/storage. For example, with ASCII, A = 01000001.

ASCII stands for American Standard Code for Information Interchange.

The computer understands only 0 and 1.

Binary vs Decimal Number Systems

Binary systemDecimal system
Base 2Base 10
Only two digits: 0 and 1Ten digits: 0 to 9
The computer's systemHumans' everyday system

A binary number can contain only 0 and 1 — so 11E is NOT a binary number, because E is not a binary digit.

Converting Between Binary and Decimal

  • Decimal 10 = 8 + 2 = binary 1010.
  • Binary 10101 = 16 + 0 + 4 + 0 + 1 = decimal 21.
  • Place values in binary (from the right): 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32...

mcqs.q: ASCII stands for:
options: American Standard Code for Information Interchange
American Scientific Character for Information Interchange
American Simple Clause for Information Interchange
American Structural Character for Information Interchange
mcqs.why: Correct answer: American Standard Code for Information Interchange. ASCII is the code that converts letters into binary, e.g. A = 01000001.

mcqs.q: Which of the following is NOT a binary number?
mcqs.why: Correct answer: 11E. Binary numbers contain only 0 and 1; E is not a binary digit, so 11E cannot be a binary number.

mcqs.q: How is information stored on the computer?
options: In binary (0 and 1) — letters, pictures and sound are encoded into binary code and stored
mcqs.why: Correct answer: In binary. With encoding, letters/pictures/sound are converted into binary code (e.g. ASCII: A = 01000001) and that code is stored in memory/storage.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between the binary and decimal number systems?
options: Binary has base 10, decimal has base 2
Binary: base 2, digits 0 and 1 (computer's system); Decimal: base 10, digits 0 to 9 (humans' system)
mcqs.why: Correct answer: Binary is base 2 with digits 0 and 1 — the computer's system. Decimal is base 10 with digits 0 to 9 — our everyday system.

mcqs.q: The base value in the binary number system is ______.
mcqs.why: Correct answer: 2. The binary system is built on base 2, which is why it has only two digits: 0 and 1.

mcqs.q: The binary equivalent of the decimal number 10 is ______.
mcqs.why: Correct answer: 1010. 10 = 8 + 2, so the 8s and 2s places are 1 and the others are 0: 1010.

mcqs.q: ______ is the decimal value of the binary number 10101.
mcqs.why: Correct answer: 21. 10101 = 16 + 0 + 4 + 0 + 1 = 21, using the binary place values 16, 8, 4, 2, 1.

mcqs.q: The computer understands only ______ and ______.
mcqs.why: Correct answer: 0 and 1. Everything — letters, pictures, sound — is first converted into binary code of 0s and 1s for the computer.

mcqs.q: In ASCII, the letter A is stored as:
mcqs.why: Correct answer: 01000001. The lesson gives this example of encoding: with ASCII, A = 01000001.

mcqs.q: Which number is a correct binary number?
mcqs.why: Correct answer: 101. A binary number may contain only the digits 0 and 1 — 12A, 210 and 1E1 all contain other digits or letters.

lessons.title: Scratch — Sprites, Blocks and Events
lessons.notes_html:
Scratch Blocks

In Scratch the building blocks are divided into 9 types (block palettes):

The 9 block types
MotionLooksSound
EventsControlSensing
OperatorsVariablesMy Blocks
  • The move 10 steps block belongs to the Motion category — it moves the sprite forward.
  • The centre of the XY plane (the stage) is X = 0, Y = 0.

Important Terms

TermMeaning
SpriteThe character or object in Scratch that moves, speaks or interacts with others (e.g. the cat)
StageThe background where all the activity happens
CostumeA different shape/appearance of the sprite — changing the costume makes the sprite look different
VariableA container/box that stores a value (such as score, name, lives, time) which can change

Events

An event is the trigger that starts a script. Examples: when green flag clicked, when sprite clicked, when a key is pressed (when space key pressed), when the backdrop switches, when a message is received. Without events a program does not start.

Reading a Scratch Script

In the book's script (when green flag clicked → go to x: 0 y: 0 → repeat until ... → move 10 steps → stop all), the block that can move the sprite to (10, 0) is move 10 steps — it moves the sprite 10 steps in the direction it faces.

mcqs.q: In Scratch, the 'move 10 steps' block belongs to which category?
mcqs.why: Correct answer: Motion. The move 10 steps block is a Motion-category block, which moves the sprite forward.

mcqs.q: ______ is the central coordinate of the XY plane.
mcqs.why: Correct answer: X=0, Y=0. The centre of the stage is (0,0) — the go to x: 0 y: 0 block places the sprite there.

mcqs.q: How many types of block palettes are there in Scratch programming?
mcqs.why: Correct answer: 9 types. They are: Motion, Looks, Sound, Events, Control, Sensing, Operators, Variables and My Blocks.

mcqs.q: A 'sprite' in Scratch is:
options: The character or object that moves, speaks or interacts with others
mcqs.why: Correct answer: The character or object, e.g. the cat. The stage is the background; the sprite is what acts on it.

mcqs.q: The 'stage' in Scratch is:
options: The background where all the activity happens
mcqs.why: Correct answer: The background where all the activity happens. Sprites move and act on the stage.

mcqs.q: A 'costume' of a sprite is:
options: A different shape/appearance of the sprite
mcqs.why: Correct answer: A different appearance of the sprite. Changing the costume makes the sprite look different, which is how walking animations are made.

mcqs.q: A 'variable' in Scratch is:
options: A container/box that stores a value (score, name, lives, time) which can change
mcqs.why: Correct answer: A container that stores a changing value. Variables hold things like score, name, lives and time in a program.

mcqs.q: What is an 'event' in Scratch?
options: The trigger that starts a script, e.g. when green flag clicked
mcqs.why: Correct answer: The trigger that starts a script. Other examples: when sprite clicked, when a key is pressed, when the backdrop switches, when a message is received. Without events a program does not start.

mcqs.q: Which block can move the sprite from (0,0) to (10,0) in the book's script?
mcqs.why: Correct answer: Move 10 steps. It moves the sprite 10 steps in the direction it faces, i.e. from (0,0) to (10,0); the green flag only starts the script.

mcqs.q: Which of these is an Events example?
mcqs.why: Correct answer: When space key pressed. Events are triggers — when green flag clicked, when sprite clicked, when a key is pressed, when a message is received.

mcqs.q: The decimal number 54 in binary is:
mcqs.why: Correct answer: 110110. 54 = 32 + 16 + 4 + 2, so the 32, 16, 4 and 2 places are 1: 110110.

mcqs.q: The binary number 1001 in decimal is:
mcqs.why: Correct answer: 9. 1001 = 8 + 1 = 9, using place values 8, 4, 2, 1.

mcqs.q: The decimal number 35 in binary is:
mcqs.why: Correct answer: 100011. 35 = 32 + 2 + 1, so only the 32, 2 and 1 places are 1.

mcqs.q: The binary number 1100 in decimal is:
mcqs.why: Correct answer: 12. Using the binary place values 8, 4, 2, 1: 1100 = 8 + 4 = 12.

mcqs.q: Which Motion block places the sprite at the centre of the stage?
mcqs.why: Correct answer: Go to x: 0 y: 0. The centre of the stage is (0,0); from there the glide block can move the sprite to the desired position.

mcqs.q: To move the sprite up with the up-arrow key, we use:
mcqs.why: Correct answer: Change y by 10. In the forever loop: up arrow → change y by 10, down arrow → change y by -10, right → change x by 10, left → change x by -10.

mcqs.q: For automatic movement across the screen, the script uses:
options: Forever → move 10 steps → if on edge, bounce
mcqs.why: Correct answer: Forever → move 10 steps → if on edge, bounce. The forever loop keeps the sprite moving and the bounce turns it at the edge.

mcqs.q: In the score activity, the Score variable is first:
options: Set to 0 when the green flag is clicked
mcqs.why: Correct answer: Set to 0. Then, forever: if touching the other sprite, change Score by 1 — and clicking the sprite also changes Score by 1.

mcqs.q: In the Scratch story-book activity, the book's pages are made from:
options: Backdrops (Backdrop 1, 2, 3) changed with the next backdrop block
mcqs.why: Correct answer: Backdrops. The sprites are the characters (cat and dog), each backdrop is a page, and the next backdrop block turns the page.

mcqs.q: The decimal number 47 in binary is:
mcqs.why: Correct answer: 101111. 47 = 32 + 8 + 4 + 2 + 1, so those places are 1 and the 16 place is 0.

lessons.title: Netiquette — Good Behaviour Online
lessons.notes_html:
What is Netiquette?

Netiquette means appropriate and respectful behaviour on the internet — the rules of good manners and etiquette in the online world:

  • Speaking politely (using polite language in messages)
  • Respecting others' opinions — respecting another person's opinion is appropriate behaviour online
  • Not sharing personal information
  • Not spreading rumours
  • Being mindful of time
  • Not hurting others, and caring for others' privacy

Appropriate vs Inappropriate Behaviour

Appropriate ✓Inappropriate ✗
Using polite language in messagesSharing someone's private pictures
Respecting another person's opinionSpreading wrong information / rumours
Caring for others' privacyIgnoring cyberbullying

mcqs.q: Which of the following is an example of appropriate online behaviour?
mcqs.why: Correct answer: Using polite language in messages. Appropriate online behaviour (netiquette) includes politeness, respect and caring for others' privacy.

mcqs.q: What does the term 'netiquette' refer to?
options: Appropriate and respectful behaviour on the internet
mcqs.why: Correct answer: Appropriate and respectful behaviour on the internet. Netiquette is the rules of good manners and etiquette in the online world.

mcqs.q: Respecting another person's opinion is an example of ______ behaviour online.
mcqs.why: Correct answer: Appropriate. Respecting others' opinions is part of netiquette, along with speaking politely and not hurting others.

mcqs.q: What is netiquette?
options: The rules of good manners and etiquette in the online world
mcqs.why: Correct answer: The rules of good manners in the online world. Netiquette includes speaking politely, respecting opinions, not sharing personal information, not spreading rumours and being mindful of time.

mcqs.q: Which of these is part of netiquette?
mcqs.why: Correct answer: Not spreading rumours. Netiquette says: be polite, respect opinions, do not share personal information, do not spread rumours, be mindful of time and do not hurt others.

mcqs.q: Sharing someone's private pictures online is:
options: A way to protect the computer
A positive effect of social media
mcqs.why: Correct answer: Inappropriate behaviour. Appropriate behaviour cares for others' privacy; sharing private pictures breaks it.

mcqs.q: 'Being mindful of time' online means:
options: Respecting others' time and not wasting it
mcqs.why: Correct answer: Respecting others' time. Being mindful of time is one of the netiquette rules listed in this lesson.

mcqs.q: Ignoring cyberbullying when we see it is:
mcqs.why: Correct answer: Inappropriate behaviour. In the book's MCQ, ignoring cyberbullying is listed with the inappropriate actions; good citizens report harmful behaviour to a trusted adult.

mcqs.q: Polite language in messages shows:
mcqs.why: Correct answer: Appropriate online behaviour. Politeness, respect and caring for privacy are the heart of netiquette.

mcqs.q: Which one should we NOT do online, according to netiquette?
mcqs.why: Correct answer: Share personal information. Netiquette clearly says not to share personal information and not to spread rumours.

lessons.title: Cyberbullying and Digital Prejudice
lessons.notes_html:
Cyberbullying

Cyberbullying is using technology (mobile, internet, social media) to repeatedly hurt, embarrass or frighten someone: bad messages, rumours, sharing private pictures, removing someone from a group, impersonation.

  • Sending a hurtful message to a classmate on game chat is cyberbullying.

Digital Prejudice

Digital prejudice means treating people unfairly online on the basis of their race, religion, gender, language or identity — e.g. removing someone from a group because of their background, or valuing their opinion less.

Rumours and Misuse

  • Spreading rumours about someone is an inappropriate and hurtful act.
  • Downloading illegal (pirated) software is an example of misuse of computer resources.

mcqs.q: What does digital prejudice mean?
mcqs.why: Correct answer: Treating people unfairly online. Digital prejudice means treating people unfairly on the basis of their race, religion, gender or identity.

mcqs.q: Sending a ______ message to a classmate on game chat is an example of cyberbullying.
mcqs.why: Correct answer: Hurtful. Sending a hurtful/bad message to a classmate is cyberbullying — using technology to hurt, embarrass or frighten someone.

mcqs.q: Spreading ______ about someone is an inappropriate act.
mcqs.why: Correct answer: Rumours. Spreading rumours about someone is an inappropriate and hurtful act, and it is also a form of cyberbullying.

mcqs.q: Downloading ______ software is an example of misuse of computer resources.
mcqs.why: Correct answer: Illegal software. Downloading illegal (pirated) software is misuse of computer resources.

mcqs.q: What is cyberbullying?
options: Using technology to repeatedly hurt, embarrass or frighten someone
mcqs.why: Correct answer: Using technology to hurt, embarrass or frighten someone repeatedly. Its forms include bad messages, rumours, sharing private pictures, removing from a group and impersonation.

mcqs.q: Which of these is an example of digital prejudice?
options: Removing someone from a group because of their background
mcqs.why: Correct answer: Removing someone from a group because of their background. Digital prejudice is unfair treatment online based on race, religion, gender, language or identity.

mcqs.q: Sharing another student's private pictures without permission is:
options: A positive effect of social media
mcqs.why: Correct answer: Cyberbullying. Sharing private pictures is one of the forms of cyberbullying listed in the lesson.

mcqs.q: Impersonation — pretending to be someone else online to harm them — is a form of:
mcqs.why: Correct answer: Cyberbullying. The lesson lists impersonation with bad messages, rumours, private pictures and group removal as cyberbullying.

mcqs.q: Removing a student from an online group to hurt them is:
mcqs.why: Correct answer: Cyberbullying. Excluding/removing someone from a group on purpose is one of the cyberbullying situations in the class activity.

mcqs.q: Treating people unfairly online because of their language or religion is called:
mcqs.why: Correct answer: Digital prejudice. It means unfair treatment online on the basis of race, religion, gender, language or identity.

lessons.title: Social Media, Safety and Computer Threats
lessons.notes_html:
Positive Effects of Social Media

A positive effect of using social media is making global friends and learning — with social media, friends can be made around the world, new things can be learned, contact with family stays, and knowledge can be shared. (Online scams, cyberbullying and the screen-time habit are negative effects.)

Protecting the Computer

  • Use antivirus software — it finds, stops and removes viruses, and helps protect the device from viruses.
  • Do NOT disable the firewall, share passwords, or open unknown email attachments.

Computer Threats

A computer threat is anything that can harm the computer, the information stored in it, or the user. Five examples:

12345
VirusMalwareHackingPhishingSpam

mcqs.q: Which is a positive effect of using social media?
mcqs.why: Correct answer: Making global friends and learning. With social media, friends can be made around the world and new things can be learned; scams, cyberbullying and screen-time habit are negative effects.

mcqs.q: Which is a proper way to protect the computer from viruses?
mcqs.why: Correct answer: Using antivirus software. Antivirus finds and stops viruses; the other three options actually make the computer unsafe.

mcqs.q: ______ software helps protect the device from viruses.
mcqs.why: Correct answer: Antivirus. Antivirus software finds and removes viruses from the device.

mcqs.q: What is a computer threat?
options: Anything that can harm the computer, the information stored in it, or the user
mcqs.why: Correct answer: Anything that can harm the computer, its information, or the user. The five examples in the book are: virus, malware, hacking, phishing and spam.

mcqs.q: Which of these is one of the five computer threats in the book?
mcqs.why: Correct answer: Phishing. The book's five threats are virus, malware, hacking, phishing and spam.

mcqs.q: Name one positive effect of using social media.
mcqs.why: Correct answer: Making global friends and learning. Social media also keeps contact with family and lets us share knowledge.

mcqs.q: Opening an unknown email attachment is:
options: Dangerous — it can bring a virus
mcqs.why: Correct answer: Dangerous. The proper protection is antivirus software; opening unknown attachments, disabling the firewall and sharing passwords are all unsafe.

mcqs.q: Spam is listed in this lesson as:
options: A positive effect of social media
One of the five computer threats
mcqs.why: Correct answer: One of the five computer threats — virus, malware, hacking, phishing and spam.

mcqs.q: Hacking means a threat to the computer because:
options: It can harm the computer or the information stored in it
mcqs.why: Correct answer: It can harm the computer or its information. That is the definition of a computer threat, and hacking is one of its five examples.

mcqs.q: Which habit protects our accounts as well as our computer?
options: Never sharing passwords and using antivirus software
mcqs.why: Correct answer: Never sharing passwords and using antivirus. Sharing passwords, disabling the firewall and opening unknown attachments are the unsafe choices in the book's question.

mcqs.q: 'Reporting cyberbullying to a trusted adult' is:

mcqs.q: 'Ignoring a friend who fell down and got hurt' is:

mcqs.why: Correct answer: Not cyberbullying. A funny video hurts no one, so it is not bullying of any kind.

options: It is done on a computer
It happens only once by accident
It is done by a teacher
It is meant to hurt, embarrass or frighten someone, repeatedly
mcqs.why: Correct answer: Harmful intent and repetition. A wrong-person message is a mistake; bad messages, embarrassing pictures and exclusion meant to hurt are cyberbullying.

lessons.title: What is Entrepreneurship?
lessons.notes_html:
What is Entrepreneurship?

Entrepreneurship means that a person identifies an opportunity and starts a new business to solve a problem. A person who starts a new business is called an entrepreneur.

Innovation

Innovation helps people change old ways of thinking and try new ways.

Product and Service

A product or service is work or help that a person provides to others to meet their needs. A product is a thing; a service is work/help.

Problem Identification

Problem identification means finding and recognising a problem or need in daily life or the community — it is the first stage of design thinking and business. Examples: litter in school, water shortage, long queues.

Origami

The art of folding paper into beautiful shapes is called origami — the Japanese art of making beautiful shapes by folding paper (an example of a creative product idea).

mcqs.q: A person who starts a new business is called?
mcqs.why: Correct answer: Entrepreneur. An entrepreneur is the person who identifies an opportunity and starts a new business to solve a problem.

mcqs.q: The art of folding paper into beautiful shapes?
mcqs.why: Correct answer: Origami. Origami is the Japanese art of making beautiful shapes by folding paper.

mcqs.q: Entrepreneurship means that a person identifies an opportunity and starts a new ______ to solve a problem.
mcqs.why: Correct answer: Business. Entrepreneurship = identifying an opportunity and starting a new business to solve a problem.

mcqs.q: Innovation helps people change ______ ways of thinking and try new ways.
mcqs.why: Correct answer: Old. Innovation helps people change old ways of thinking and try new ways of doing things.

mcqs.q: A ______ or service is work or help that a person provides to others to meet their needs.
mcqs.why: Correct answer: Product. The lesson's sentence is: a product or service is work or help provided to others to meet their needs — a product is a thing, a service is work.

mcqs.q: What is problem identification?
options: Finding and recognising a problem or need in daily life or the community
mcqs.why: Correct answer: Finding and recognising a problem or need. It is the first stage of design thinking and business — e.g. litter in school, water shortage, long queues.

mcqs.q: Which of these is an example of problem identification?
options: Buying a finished product from a shop
Noticing litter in the school and the need for cleanliness
mcqs.why: Correct answer: Noticing litter in school. Problem identification means finding a real problem or need — the book's examples are litter in school, water shortage and long queues.

mcqs.q: An entrepreneur starts a new business mainly to:
options: Solve a problem by identifying an opportunity
mcqs.why: Correct answer: Solve a problem. Entrepreneurship begins with an opportunity found in a problem or need of people.

mcqs.q: Which of these is a service, not a product?
options: Home delivery of groceries — work a person does for others
mcqs.why: Correct answer: Home delivery service. A product is a thing that can be bought and touched; a service is work or help a person provides.

mcqs.q: Origami products could be sold by an entrepreneur because origami is:
options: The art of folding paper into beautiful shapes that people may buy
mcqs.why: Correct answer: An art that makes beautiful paper shapes. The lesson uses origami as an example of a creative skill that can become a product.

lessons.title: Design Thinking and Product Stages
lessons.notes_html:
Design Thinking

Design thinking is a creative method for solving real-life problems, step by step. Its process has these stages:

StageMeaning
1. IdentifyFind the problem
2. EmpathizeFeel others' problem
3. DefineState the problem clearly
4. IdeateThink of new ideas
5. PrototypeMake a model
6. TestTest whether it works or not
7. ReflectLearn from feedback
8. IterateImprove the product on the basis of feedback and try again

Then comes Implementation — the stage where a real business starts selling finished products to customers.

Key Words

  • Prototype — a model or sample of a product (the first model).
  • Test stage — the stage where a product or idea is tested whether it works or not.
  • Improvement (Iterate) stage — the stage where the product is improved on the basis of feedback.

mcqs.q: The stage where a product or idea is tested whether it works or not?
mcqs.why: Correct answer: Test. In the Test stage a product or idea is tested whether it works correctly or not.

mcqs.q: A model or sample of a product is called?
mcqs.why: Correct answer: Prototype. A prototype is the first model or sample of a product, made before the real product.

mcqs.q: Design thinking is a ______ method for solving real-life problems.
mcqs.why: Correct answer: Creative. Design thinking is a creative, step-by-step method for solving problems.

mcqs.q: The stage where the product is improved on the basis of feedback is called ______.
mcqs.why: Correct answer: Improvement (Iterate). After testing and reflecting on feedback, the product is improved and tried again — that is iteration.

mcqs.q: What is the name of the stage where a real business starts selling finished products to customers?
mcqs.why: Correct answer: Implementation. In the Implementation stage the business starts selling the finished product to real customers in the market.

mcqs.q: What is the design thinking process?
options: Identify → Empathize → Define → Ideate → Prototype → Test → Reflect → Iterate
mcqs.why: Correct answer: The 8-stage process. Find the problem, feel it, state it clearly, think of ideas, make a model, test it, learn from feedback, improve — then Implementation.

mcqs.q: The first stage of design thinking, 'Identify', means:
mcqs.why: Correct answer: Find the problem. Identifying the problem comes first — the same as problem identification in entrepreneurship.

mcqs.q: 'Empathize' in design thinking means:
mcqs.why: Correct answer: Feel others' problem. Empathizing helps us understand what people really need before defining the problem.

mcqs.q: After the Test stage, feedback is used in which stage?
options: Reflect — learn from feedback, then Iterate to improve
mcqs.why: Correct answer: Reflect, then Iterate. We learn from feedback (Reflect) and improve the product on its basis (Iterate) before implementation.

mcqs.q: A prototype is made in which stage?
mcqs.why: Correct answer: Stage 5. The order is: Identify, Empathize, Define, Ideate, Prototype (make a model), Test, Reflect, Iterate.

lessons.title: Global Goals and Solving Daily Problems
lessons.notes_html:
Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)

The United Nations has made 17 special goals — the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) — for the world.

  • Goal 1: No Poverty — aimed at ending every form of poverty in the world.

Problem-Solving in Daily Life — Five Examples

ProblemSolution
Broken tapFit a new tap
Forgetting homeworkMake a checklist
Dark roomFit a lamp/light
Litter in schoolDustbins and a cleanliness campaign
Long queueA token system

These examples show that entrepreneurship begins at home and school: find a problem, think of a solution, and act on it.

mcqs.q: How many special goals has the United Nations made?
mcqs.why: Correct answer: 17. The United Nations has 17 Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).

mcqs.q: What is Sustainable Development Goal number 1 aimed at ending?
mcqs.why: Correct answer: Poverty. Goal 1 (No Poverty) aims to end every form of poverty in the world.

mcqs.q: For the problem 'forgetting homework', the book's solution is:
mcqs.why: Correct answer: Make a checklist. Each daily problem has a matching solution: broken tap → new tap; dark room → lamp; litter → dustbins and campaign; long queue → token system.

mcqs.q: For a long queue, the book suggests:
mcqs.why: Correct answer: A token system. Tokens organise the queue so everyone is served in turn.

mcqs.q: For litter in school, the solution given is:
mcqs.why: Correct answer: Dustbins and a cleanliness campaign. This is one of the five daily-life problem-solving examples in the lesson.

mcqs.q: A dark room can be solved by:
mcqs.why: Correct answer: Fitting a lamp/light. The pattern of the lesson: every problem has a practical solution — broken tap → fit a new tap, dark room → fit a lamp.

mcqs.q: The SDG goals were made by:
mcqs.why: Correct answer: The United Nations. It made 17 special goals — the Sustainable Development Goals — for the whole world.

mcqs.q: Which of these pairs (problem → solution) is correct?
mcqs.why: Correct answer: Long queue → token system. The other correct pairs are: broken tap → new tap; dark room → lamp; forgetting homework → checklist; litter → dustbins and campaign.

mcqs.q: These daily-life examples teach that problem-solving starts with:
options: Finding and recognising a real problem
mcqs.why: Correct answer: Finding a real problem. Every example begins with a problem people actually face — that is problem identification, the first stage of design thinking and business.

mcqs.q: Goal 1 of the SDGs is called:
mcqs.why: Correct answer: No Poverty. Sustainable Development Goal number 1 aims to end every form of poverty in the world.

lessons.title: Entrepreneurship Activities
lessons.notes_html:
Class Activity 1 — Product vs Service

Problem given: "People need help getting groceries delivered home."

  • Product solution: a grocery cart — a thing that can be bought, seen and touched.
  • Service solution: a home delivery service — work that a person does, cannot be seen.
  • Difference: a product is a thing; a service is work/help.

Group Activity 2 — "Problem Finders" Scavenger Hunt

Teams take a notebook and pencil, visit a place (classroom, library, playground), find things that do not work correctly, write the problems, and discuss: "Why is this a problem for people?"

Problem foundSolution
Finding a book in the library is difficultLabels/list on books
The chairs are too small or uncomfortableRight-sized chairs
The dustbin in the classroom is far awayKeep a bin nearby
The water tap on the playground is brokenRepair the tap

These are problems for people because they make daily work difficult and slow. The activity teaches us to understand people's feelings (empathize) and the importance of solving problems.

mcqs.q: In the grocery activity, a grocery cart is an example of a:
options: Product — a thing that can be bought, seen and touched
mcqs.why: Correct answer: A product. A product is a thing; the home delivery of groceries is the service — work a person does.

mcqs.q: A home delivery service is different from a product because:
options: It is work/help a person does, not a thing
mcqs.why: Correct answer: It is work, not a thing. That is the difference the activity teaches: product = thing, service = work/help.

mcqs.q: In the 'Problem Finders' activity, teams carry:
options: A notebook and pencil to write the problems they find
mcqs.why: Correct answer: A notebook and pencil. Each group visits a place like the classroom, library or playground and writes down the things that do not work correctly.

mcqs.q: 'Finding a book in the library is difficult' — the model solution is:
mcqs.why: Correct answer: Labels/list on books. Each found problem gets a matching simple solution — right-sized chairs, a nearby bin, repairing the broken tap.

mcqs.q: The Problem Finders discussion question is:
options: 'Why is this a problem for people?'
mcqs.why: Correct answer: 'Why is this a problem for people?' These problems make daily work difficult and slow — understanding that is empathizing with people.

mcqs.q: The classroom dustbin being far away is solved by:
mcqs.why: Correct answer: Keeping a bin nearby. The activity matches each problem with its own practical solution.

mcqs.q: The Problem Finders activity mainly teaches:
options: To observe real places, find people's problems and understand their feelings
mcqs.why: Correct answer: Observing and empathizing. The teacher explains that the activity helps students learn about understanding people's feelings and the importance of solving problems.

mcqs.q: Uncomfortable, too-small chairs in the library are a problem because they:
options: Make daily work difficult and slow for people
mcqs.why: Correct answer: They make daily work difficult and slow. That is why such things count as problems worth solving in the activity's discussion.

mcqs.q: Which of these found problems matches the solution 'repair the tap'?
options: The water tap on the playground is broken
mcqs.why: Correct answer: The broken playground water tap. Each problem in the model completion has its own solution — tap broken → repair the tap.

mcqs.q: The grocery problem ('people need help getting groceries delivered home') can be solved by:
options: A product (cart) or a service (delivery) — both are valid solutions
mcqs.why: Correct answer: Both. The activity's point is that one problem can have a product solution and a service solution — groups explain how they differ.
